I remember when I first found out about this game, I thought of it as dumb. I was still a raging teenager only thinking about how manly I should be, as a man. Why would someone as manly as me play something clearly designed for little girls? A mermaid singing in caves of - ugh! - COLORFUL FLOWERS!!! In the beginning speech, the mermaid's speaking like she's reading a poem! What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥! Also, this bacon slab is hella manly and tasty!
Okay, that's an exaggeration. I did think of Aquaria as something dumb and girly at first, but I still decided to try it. I can no longer remember why, but I'm sure it was simply that Aquaria did, indeed, look very interesting. Before that point I had only played games without thinking about them too much, so I had a rather shallow image of video games.
I remember when I started a new game. I remember the feeling after the opening speech, how Naija was sitting on the rock, how the light was pouring down from the cracks at the ceiling... and, oh gods, the music. A piece that is like a lullaby for a baby, yet it indeed does give a feeling of emptiness, of loneliness. And as basic human instincts decide to fight these feelings, I went on to the other side of the cave to find something, anything that would make me feel whole.
How shameless of the muscular me. It was as if I was living in Naija's world! Quick, pass me the protein shake and my weights.
To sing, you hold the right mouse button down. A circle of 8 symbols will appear. The lowermost symbol is the highest pitch you can do, and the one to the immediate right is the lowest, and all the other symbols inbetween clockwise are the rest of the tones. So, to sing, you simply move your mouse atop one of the symbols while holding the right mouse button down. A bit later in to the game you'll get "songs" to sing that make Naija do all kinds of stuff, mostly transforming into something else such as the energy form that shoots blasts of energy, or the beast mode that allows you to eat other fauna.
That's the way you'll be doing combat and solving puzzles. You're also (obviously) underwater, so you can move to all directions however you wish. Under these gameplay mechanics a world was made, which is yours to explore. You'll be going in a kingdom with a necessary castle-like building for its rulers, overrun by disgusting creatures; to the surface to feel the sun's warm rays for the first time in your life; and to the depths of the sea, the abyss. Aquaria may not have a procedurally generated universe, but that's what it makes amazing - all the areas you see have been carefully crafted, their enemies placed where they belong with many secrets hidden around. In each area there's a lot to explore, and there's even a whole area as a secret! For your first playthrough you may even miss a large amount of content.
What wonders will I find in the light ahead? What kind of horrors will appear around the corner? Aquaria changed my mind about what games can really be. It was an indie game before the time of Kickstarters or Greenlights... I can only imagine how much the developers had to go through to get the game out the way they wanted while making profits of it.
I still see Aquaria as something that has yet to grow mold compared to the newer games. The gameplay is still fresh and graphics are beautiful... although admittedly, the animation are rather awkward and clunky at times (everyone who's played through the game should be reminded about the final boss' death scene about now). But that's a minor offence compared to everything else amazing in this piece of art.
- Beautiful graphics and music blended to one, as if a painting dragging you into its world, both visually and mentally
- A huge world to explore. Not the procedurally generated kind that roguelikes and other up-and-coming exploration games do, so whatever you find in this game is definitely worth its time.
- An interesting combat system with many enemies bosses to test it on. However I must admit that some bosses felt too much like puzzle bosses
- But also fun and well thought-out puzzles that aren't bosses! Using the singing system, obviously.
- A coming-of-age story, in a way. Filling the emptiness inside via traveling and finding the wonders (and horrors) of the world
Now, after I've written this "review," I notice that it's more like me simply being reminiscent. I hope you don't mind, Aquaria means a lot to me as a gamer. Still, I assure you that it's not simply nostalgia or favoriting, I'm sure if you're an avid gamer you'll be enjoying this game a lot.
P.S. I actually was a scrawny teenager with non-existent muscles and a girlish face, and I didn't (still don't) like bacon by itself

Had this game via Humble Bundle ages ago, I finally decided to play it.
My final review is "Nice game, just not my kind of game".
The game mechanic revolves around explorationm, using only the mouse (there is gamepad support anyway), and learning "songs", a-la-Ocarina of time, that will unlock powers and new forms for the protagonist. Controls sometimes feel stiff and they probably didn't age that well (the game is from 2007!), but the overall experience is not bad. The crafting system is great and not too much complicated, very balanced.
The map is big and well constructed: you can be immersed without necessairly get "lost" and frustrated. The art is good but a bit repetitive, except some good levels and boss fights.
While I cannot say if the story is any good (I've left the game WAAAY before finishing it), I have to admit that I didn't feel like it mattered that much. It starts with the protagonist mermaid trying to find out her past and what happened to its civilization, but it soon starts feeling more like a plot device than a real story. I know this may apply to EVERY story ever told in a videogame, but on the other side this might just be me.
Overall, yes, it's a good game and I would recommend it to the fans of the genre. Sadly, even though I really wanted to like it, I didn't feel invested enough to complete it or even to go through a very big part of it. When I stumbled upon the lenght of the experience (12 to 15 hours) my mind just yelled "Yeah, not worth that much time".
It's good, anyway!

You can't jump backwards, and you're stuck in your parabola from the moment you start your ascent. You might stick your landing, or you might slide all the way back down. Of course, when reaching a floating bubble of water, because why not, ♥♥♥♥ physics, momentum is not just conserved, no, you freaking accelerate. So you fall down, all the way back to the beginnning, to start another infuriating round of special olympics rock climbing. So you better hit the brakes (no stop button, you have to continuously click, like in Dota, to get anywhere). And in order to do that quickly, you have to "boost".
Boosting in general is a crapshoot, because if you hit a wall you stick to it and grab on, because you totally need to do that... for nothing. Occasionally you can grab onto larger enemies and ... ride them. Still haven't figured out how to do that with the sea horses though, which might be helpful, although the fish form is supposed to be decently speedy on it's own.
The map is an uninformative mess. You can barely scroll in, leading to the persisting question "is this a map for ants?". Due to the litany of secret passages that don't become more noticable when crossing them, or screwy pocket dimension spaces, the map is all sort of overlapped on itself, which makes decyphering it a chore. Landmarks are few and far between, so hopefully you remembered to mark any weird areas on your map that you might want to come back to. I don't recall seeing a legend on the map, so it's just a bunch of meaningless symbols until you figure out what green testicles marker means (apparently if you throw a seed at them they open up). They do have an option to place markers, but really, that should be done automatically. Quest markers would have been nice too, I detected a tell tale shimmer of purple on the second level, why didn't that continue? That was obviously a mechaninc that just didn't get implemented, at least give me a hint as to where to go.
The sound track is repetitive to the point that I think it might have been initially designed as an enhanced interrogation technique. Most of the "music" is two or three measures long, and on an endless loop. No songs can be described as catchy, just mind numbing. At no point did I want to explore the attached OST, nor do I know of why anyone would want to subject themselves to that.
Farming items, which is necessary after every boss fight, is a massive hassle. You can't trade/ buy items (there aren't really any NPC's beside you and your deaf/mute boyfriend) and there is a maximum amount of each item in your inventory, so you can't stock up past 8 of anything. Most items have maybe one or 2 recipes they can be used in, with the exception of some stock items that you will be in continuous short supply of (leaves, eggs, and occasionally oils). Cooking is repetitive, you can't just macro it and make 8 of the same item, no, you painstakingly drag each ingredient. You need to conult the fan made guides to get recipes to cook, because if you do it blindly, you'll waste ingredients. Instead of just saying recipe not found, or having a system whereby you learn recipes ahead of time (you sort of do that when you find cooked items in the field), you can attempt to mix things together, but usually you end up with something useless. Most of the cooked items are useless to begin with. For instance, shroom soup. Let's mess with your screen to the point the game isn't playable and make sounds like your dying, because we're edgey but don't know the effects of psylocybin.
Most of the forms/ powerups you obtain are gimmicky and useless, and you'll end up mainly using the energy form. The song form can pretty much be replaced by hotkeys, although the urchin armor (armors apparently can only be worn by your song form) can be used to break the octopus boss. Beast form is unweildy, the lunge has a long recharge, you don't get items dropped by enemies that you kill, and for some reason you don't get health returned from eating the enemy unless it's a certain jellyfish, that usually drop health when you kill them anyway. Nature form can open some doors and avoid damage from certain environmental hazards, but the spiky flower cactus thing has a long charge time making it kind of useless for anything. The light form barely works, and can sort of be replaced by the glowing octopus pet, but both are pretty crappy to begin with. You can charge it up to make the area slightly brighter, but useless in combat. Fish is sort of fast and is used for gimmicky passages, same with the spirit form. There is an item so you can attack with the fish, but honestly, you might as well use energy form constantly, except when you need to bing/ move something, which is the one thing I haven't found a hot key for. Hot keys for everything, including spinning in place, which has so far been used in one location. I guess if bind had a hot key the song form would be totally redundant.
The forms are mainly used to chase gimmicky collectibles where aren't needed in the least. Their sole function is to slightly spruce up your crappy grotto home, in the same way that a "hang in there" poster would make your skid row apartment not make you want to hang yourself. Which is to say, barely. The pot of meat/ bag of seeds do speed up the farming bit a tad though, although it would be nice when pulling out plants, which you need to bind every single time, to not have a randomized loot system with dud options. I don't need small bones (I like how recipes call for "any bone" or "any shroom" or "any berry", as there is just one of each type), or better yet, small enemies that attack you. It just makes farming that much more of a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
There is no quicksave option, there are no menu options to save. Just irregularly, semihidden save crystals...? That you have to be mindful of when exploring. Hopefully you don't get in over your head, or your time will have been wasted, because if you die, all your progress will have been lost till your last save. Which I guess is good if you just blew through all your items on a boss fight, because that's a real possibility, but kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ if you just had to make a trek to fight the boss in the first place, which quite a few bosses require.
There isn't much character development of the main character aside from painfully acted lines about this amateur fantasy world the creator has developed, in a mid atlantic accent from a cringingly badly named protagonist (Naija?). Your... boyfriend? that you almost killed because you had a rom-com introduction where you nearly drowned him then kissed him which magically made him breath in water/ want to eat raw fish never speaks, does minimal damage, and doesn't distract the various enemies, and gets stuck so often you're given a song to summon him, but can't dismiss him if you wanted to. It became a bit of a problem when trying to do the simon-says boss, when the protagonists decided to make out and float around freely while I was trying to keep up with another rage inducing bull♥♥♥♥♥♥gimmicky optional boss.

First of all, I am a big fan of mechs game.
I had played other front mission game, armored core, super robot war, some of the gundam, and I won't miss any chance to play a game that let me take control of a giant robot, so when I finally able to find steam card in my area, the first thing I do is to press the purchase button, in this game.
This turn out to be a pretty bad decision.
I am not even going to talk about the crash I am having, that should not be a part of any game review.
Let talk about the game play.
Customization
The game allow you to customize you mechs beofre mssion, which is great, as I enjoy the ability to make your own mechs and this is one of the reason that drawn me to this game. Sadly ,the customization system are done pretty wrong:
1. There are a serious lack of part to choose from
2. There are not really a good reason to customize except to put on stronger armor and weapon
3. There are no reason to use weaker "low ranked" parts anymore after you gotten better stuff.
4. In some stage they even force you to use certain part

Gameplay
Linear level, I don't even need my brain to play this game, all I do is follow the path, kill everyone, go to the next area, kill everyone and repeat, I don't even need to bother with aiming, it is better to just keep shooting, as the battlefield are small, and the enemy appear only when you are closing by, rendering long range weaponary obsolete.
There are also some problem with the game's camera, stuff like plant and tree and stuff can go between your mechs and the camera so you can't see what is going on in the battlefield.
The difficulty seem artifical to me, All boss have ton of health, and kill you in a few shot, to stay alive to do some damage you have to keep picking power up
Ally AI
The AI of ally in this game are pretty weak, to a point I didn't notice their existence until the battle of a giant mobile fortress (sorry for the possible spoiler), where for the first time i figured that I need help and fall back to them, only to find them launching missile at the wall, forcing me to deal with the boss alone.
Ally
From what I know about Front mission, It is always about coordinating with your ally and slowly yet effectively take out you enemy one by one, and this game done exactly the opposite, telling you, a civilian engineer to take on an army of mechs alone.
Human stage
Come on, this should be a game that I fight the enemy inside a giant robot, if I want to play man vs man battle, I will go get battlefield or something else.
Unlike mechs stage, There are never enough ammo.
Story
Too short, Too shallow, too light
The bad guy don't really have a good reason to fight, and the "good" side seem strangely lack the power to fight back, come on, it is suppose to be the milltary force of a whole country! and all you can spare is a few mechs? you got to be kidding me.

I had high hopes for Dungeon of the Endless as I really enjoyed the demo released a while back. It had great premise just like many other difficult procedurally generated dungeon crawlers.
Starting with the graphics and overall audio-visual quality of the game. Retro pixel art looks good, sound effects are ok with pleasant sci-fi tunes in the background. The overall feel is ok. The user interface however has some problems. It is sometimes hard to use and overall not the most user-friendly nor the best looking one I have seen lately. There are no options to resize the hud and there are only two states of map zooming, normal and tactical overview. There are problems selecting and grouping the heroes at times. Moving heroes room by room can also be a chore sometimes due to the restrictions of their movement. In the end, it has it flaws but playable.
There is enough amount of content to worth the many tries while eventually reaching the exit. Hero factions, classes, stats, leveling up, active and passive skills, and equipment adds a lot to customization options. The four resources which can be gathered via various factories are each useful for different situations and requires tactical awareness right from the beginning of the levels because the placing order of the responding module. Some of the heroes also has operate ability which further enhances a selected modules producing capability. There are randomly spawning heroes who can be recruited, and various type of merchants who sell and buy goods. The random factor is really strong however, in fact too much. The fourth resource, dust, is only used for powering rooms, which prevents enemies spawning into them and of course powers installed modules. The main problem is that dust is gained randomly by entering rooms. After a few rooms opened there are usually a shortage of dust which means that many rooms remain unpowered. When waves are spawning every unpowered room is a potential spawn point for waves which basically multiplies the number of enemies. This can cause fatal amount of foes to spawn at one given door opening. This is where a good team is essential. There are classes which are good for either tank, speedster or operator duties. They can also be strengthened via various equipments. In my latest game I had two operators, one tank and one speedster. Escapes at the end of the levels were quite easy with a 61 speed unit running with the crystal. During the levels my tank could easily gather all the mobs around him with the aggro passive skill. Eeverything was ideal, my heroes were pretty high level. There are one more thing that I would mention, and that is the personal story part. Every hero has at least one story which activates if one other member has the same one. One that I had was between a prisoner and a crew member which ended up badly. After each floor there is a small dialog sequence which cannot be skipped. I just finished the 10th floor when my speedster just killed my tank in the elevator ending their personal storyline. Now, I left with a crippled team basically at the end of the dungeon. This is that kind of (kinda) randomness which is really frustrating. I cannot finish the game as my beefed up hero got killed because some personal affair. Also, all his expensive items are lost in the process.
Overall, I will not say that this game is bad, it is just one of those titles which are going too far with their random events. It encourages multiple playthroughs, has many heroes and ships which also adds variability, but ultimately too unforgiving to offer enjoyment without constant frustration. I would recommend it but only for those who are really into this kind of game.

I'm not a rogue-like fan.  So take what I say with a grain of salt.
Pros:
- Decide what you want to build to boost science, production or food output
- But there's a break-even cost associated depending on how many doors any level has
- It's also possible to get infinite food and production with just the right technologies at an early enough level
- The tower defense element of the game is a really great twist.
- The story-line connection with other Endless games is compelling.
Cons:
- Even with maxed out characters all at level 15, by the 9th floor sometimes there just wasn't enough energy to light up rooms and it became impossible to defend the crystal.  This gave me the impression the game is purely luck of the draw - if you don't get good dice rolls, skill won't matter.
- There are many red-herring technologies and part of the game is learning how the game will play at the higher floors.  The learning curve is a bit like a very enormous "Simon" memory game - repeat the buttons until your memorize them, only here you are memorizing the relevant technologies.
- Almost won't play at all on my MacBook Pro - I have to back off the screen resolution or it's completely broken!
So even though I feel I got my money's worth, and I might play more, I don't feel there's much redeeming value to the game.  It's a bit stupid that way.  I keep asking myself "is this gameplay really very rewarding" and often the answer is no - it feels like more of a grind.
Nevertheless, I watch Amplitude's Unite 2014 video where they explain how they made the game and it was great food for thought.  It's a HORRIFYINGLY inefficent.  They show how they came up with shader solutions to some problems, and then neglected to use those same solutions for utilizing a perspective camera at long-range and instead opted for orthogonal.  So close - and they just gave up and shipped it with an orthogonal view.  This makes me cringe a little bit every time I play it - that there's so much being missed and potential the game had and it was lost.
TL:DR
If you are only going to buy 1 rogue-like, this is not it.

The toughest and most satisfying puzzle game I've ever played. Not for the faint of heart (or brain).

The empty grey background stares back at you, taunting you. You respond by filling the screen with instructions and criss-crossing paths, but it's not enough, there's still something missing.
"Maybe it will all make sense in the morning" you lie to yourself as you try, in vain, to fall asleep. You can hear it, laughing at you, mocking you for your failure. "No," you shout "I know exactly what to do, I just need to synch it so that... but no, I don't have enough room!... Unless...?"
Epiphany! It all makes sense now! How could you be so stupid, it's so simple.
Atoms and molecules are carried all across the screen in an hypnotic dance, carriers are exchanged, bonds are broken and reformed. You grin madly at your success, but as you watch your construction form and disassemble molecules, you realize you could cut out a few cycles by moving that instruction that way, and maybe if you rearrange those arrows you'll be able to cut out that overly complex loop.
And it starts anew!

So the game does get kind of boring as you progress. There isn't much reward for winning besides in-game medals and Steam achievements, if you're into that.
I will say that the graphics are gorgeous though. The planes are well designed. The levels have great texturing. But there is an over abundance of particles which I think is the cause of some serious stuttering, which is the main reason why I'm done with this game. The serious stuttering almost makes it unbearable as the frame rate drops far below the already locked 30 fps and the plane becomes uncontrollable, causing you to crash and lose your position. Although it's fairly easy to get your space back.
Another thing, this game is best suited to play with a controller. I tried playing with a kb/m, and a 360 controller was just so much more natural.
I wouldn't recommend the game though. There are many other racing games that have way more levels to try out. There's only so much you can do with the same 4 levels.
6.0/10

I've been playing since Kate and Baldspot made their debut, and it's just been a cluster.  The most common counterargument for continued support of this game is "but it has so much potential!"  Does the game have potential?  Sure it does, but like the vast majority of indie games (especially with the now infamous taglines of "Early Access Open World Survival game") out there, having a lot of potential doesn't make you special anymore.  Too many games have come through with "great potential" and ended up as vaporware or just broken messes in development hell.  Having potential shouldn't be the metric with which games are recommended, because it apparently doesn't mean jack♥♥♥♥♥♥  Furthermore, don't let the PZ updates fool you; the devs are in constant communication with their weekly mondoids, but it's a whole bunch of nothing.  Feel free to peruse some of the posts from a year or two or three or four ago that mention NPC progress, those are the best ones.
So taking an attitude of "how is the game at this very moment, without any future updates taken into consideration," can I recommend the game in it's current state for $15?  No, not really.  It's fun for a while, until you realize the gameplay really isn't that complex at the moment and there's not too much to do, and unlike other games that can be described as "mile wide and an inch deep," PZ isn't even that wide.  Maybe 20m wide and an inch deep, not a mile though.
I'd love to be proven wrong and get the chance to flip the thumb right-side up, but at this rate there's a good chance I'll have died of old age by then.

On paper, this idea of this game sounds awesome. A karate simulator where you work your way up from small beginnings. Start with training, move on to winning tournaments and money, learning new skills, and eventually opening your own dojo. Old school Neo Geo style graphics and soundtrack as icing on the cake? Sold.
Sadly, this is NOT that game.
It's a poorly translated, buggy mess.
The bulk of the first half of your journey is a handful of mini games, with fighting thrown in every now and then.
When you start out and you need money to enter tournaments? A work mini game where you drive your forklift back and forth to load a truck.
Leveling up one of your attributes? You have to play one of 20 different mini games, 4 for each one of your attributes. Many of them involve mashing buttons.
Get injured during a fight and sent to the hospital? Another mini game.
The fighting itself is pretty simplistic, resulting in a "paper, rock, scissors" of low, medium and high attacks. It's pretty brutal early on with quite a few trips to the hospital and laughably easy later, when you are powerful enough to end a fight in only 3 kicks. Worse, you're fighting the same people all throughout the game, so while your skill has increased 10 fold, everyone else has stayed at the same level.
The story bits are painful to read because of the poor translation, and not in an "All your base are belong to us" kind of way either, it's just hard to follow what's going on. In addition to that, there seem to be two different art styles clashing in the game. There is some pretty good pixel art of the fighers during gameplay, and some MSPAINT abominations during the cutscenes.
Good points: The impact of the fighting does feel good when you land a solid blow, if a bit random. The blood and bone breaking scenes are a nice touch and make you feel pretty badass.
Bad: Everything else.

I've been Playing The Long Dark for over 3 Years. I certainly have more then 134.5 Hours on record as the time of this Writing. In specificity Real Winter Survival Techniques apply to this Game with Huge results. That said real world Winter Survival isn't exactly like this game. One factor this game doesn't take into account is how much Heat the Ground can leech out of your Body. I Survived a Night in an Snow Cave/Trench Shelter at 5500 Feet on a Mountain, and compared to say 4 Inches of Snow on the Ground it was the 4 inches of Snow on the Ground that was the Most Dangerous. Plus that night my Wife, and I went out together with our Instructors, and they wanted us to crash in a Tiny Lean Too shelter that in truth would have worked...But the Ground was Lopped sided, it was Cramped as hell, and my Wife wouldn't be able to take it. So I'm like alright...I'm gonna go Camp out under a Tarp...Sat there for about 3 Hours trying to go to sleep, but my Body kept saying GET UP NOW...and when it became inescapably obvious that I was losing heat via Ground Conduction despite having a Ground pad, and a Sleeping Bag.
Probably the Worst part was the Fact I was starting to get Mildly Hypoxic because I was so congested I couldn't breath, and I was also worried about rolling over into my Tarp, and Suffocating...Fortunately we were only 200 yards from our House so that was a Bonus ended up Sleeping on my Couch warm, and Cozy, and truthfully Survival should always be seen as the best return on your Time, and Energy for the least amount of Effort. When we overcome that Adversity we begin to make those Dividend Reinvestments that Makes Civilization possible, and one thing any Serious Long Dark Player will notice is there is a Rubicon one passes in which your available available Resources increases exponentially.
The Key thing is Dividend Reinvestments.
Make small investments of your Time. Grab a Little Wood, Build a small Fire, Harvest a Little Meat, and Keep moving, and know when your about to exhaust your sustainable environment.
Highly recommended.

I haven't played the original, so my experience is solely with this version. I will get a few things out of the way: the voice acting, plot, Cat Lady.
1. Voice Acting: In the prologue, the voices are awful. In the main plot, the protagonist is almost always awful. There is a big difference in microphone quality between characters, which is sometimes quite distracting. It was so offputting, I almost stopped the game. As the game went on however, I found that I enjoyed everyone else's voice acting, which was a blessing.
2. Plot: I do feel the story borrows maybe a bit too heavily from Silent Hill 2, stepping beyond mere homage. Your protagonist's background feels sort of overdone, given the central narrative, and probably could have been made more subtle or taken out entirely. Sometimes it feels like a cheesey b-movie, other times it takes itself pretty seriously.
3. Cat Lady: I'd argue that you need to play Cat Lady first in order to understand what happens near the end of the game. I had actually played it before, but not recently, and found myself scratching my head at the references. It also doesn't fit in that well to the plot and - again - should probably have been taken out entirely.
YET I RECOMMEND IT. The art quality is a bit dicey, but it works with the atmosphere. Navigation, controls, inventory - I wasn't sure about any of these at first, but it's easy to pick up and I actually think it's a good system for a 2D world like this. The most important thing is that the puzzles were more fun than tedious; they were morbid, creative, helped you get into the game's sense of logic and were even humorous at times. For all its similarities to Silent Hill 2, the story turned out better than I expected and does manage to stand on its own.
TL;DR A bit messy at times, but overall quite entertaining.

I enjoyed Downfall way more than anticipated. In fact, I completed it in a single sitting, and had a lot of fun playing it "local co-op" with a friend. It's now in my top 2 games from 2016. Like The Cat Lady, it contains fresh and interesting narrative, twists, a focused pace with good sense of progress, endearing characters, solid puzzle design, atmospheric soundtrack (tons of music as well as ambiance), just enough dark humor, and ridiculous amounts of gore.
Also like The Cat Lady, mental illness features prominently. This time it's body dysmorphia and eating disorders, and although this can be depressing along the way, that's not necessarily where it ends up. In other words, it's mature, you've been warned, and it's worth seeing through to the end.
Another thing worth mentioning (and I feel bad for name-dropping in every single paragraph), is this remake contains far more than passing references to The Cat Lady, and although it's not critical, I think it would make more sense if you'd played The Cat Lady first. Did I mention The Cat Lady is one of my favorite games ever?
I guess I'm supposed to give critique to pretend like I'm a balanced journalist or something, and not just some guy on his couch. The truth is I just really liked Downfall all the way through. If I could change one thing, it would be for it to use a more modern game engine because this one inherently means relatively low resolution art and technical issues for a greater than average portion of players. This has been addressed for Lorelai (the final game in the trilogy).

Hard to be decent when you first start out, but once you become adept at the game's core mechanics, you will have a grand time! The bullet snaps, whistling of artillery, whines of mortars, and shouts of courage or fear from your teammates easily have a gravitating effect of pulling you into the world. When every man counts, the matches can get exceptionally close. While the game has a heavy emphasis on teamwork, and communication, even just one player can make the difference between a victory or defeat.
Whether playing Rising Storm (Pacific Theater), Red Orchestra 2 (Russians versus Germans), or the Heroes of the West mod (Americans versus Germans), you will always feel like you are in the middle of the action. The emphasis of roles in the game account for the game's versatility to suit any fps fan. Snipers main job is to take out enemy machine guns, while machine gunners suppress the enemy, and keep an area pinned down. Squad Leaders act as mobile spawn points for their squad with Squad Leader 1 being the single most important role in the game. The Team Leader directs the platoon in battle plans, calls in recon planes to reveal enemy positions, and fire support when, and where needed. Lastly is the Rifleman. The Rifleman is the backbone of the platoon responsible for eliminating enemies, but moreso for obtaining the objective. No matter how you like to play fps games, this one will have a role for you.
The beautiful scenary, historic maps, accurate weapons, and sense of comradery granted by the small, yet passionate community gives the game the most exhilerating gameplay, and experience of any fps I have played. While you hide behind a building waiting for your commander's order to push the enemy, your squadmate is behind cover, yet exposing himself enough to engage the enemy, when all of a sudden he gets hit. As he is lying on the ground slowly dying in agony, crying for his mother, your commander orders everyone to attack. Not for the faint of heart, the game will bring you to the battlefield if you let it.

红色管弦乐队，据说二战德国有一支反纳粹的秘密队伍就叫红色管弦乐队（1933-1942），制作组将游戏名命名为此，应该也有一些纪念的意思，提醒玩家们不要因为本游戏而崇尚暴力与战争。游戏中的许多地图，都是制作组参照历史多方考察而制成（GrainElevator地图中的大楼至今仍在俄罗斯可以找到）。不得不说，这款游戏真的对得起当初剁手的20美刀。断断续续玩了不少时间，写一些感受吧。
很多人把这款游戏当作二战Fps来打，几乎只在意自己一局游戏的击杀数，把击杀作为了游戏的唯一乐趣。作为射击游戏，枪法固然重要。但是，在多人游戏中，游戏的核心却是双方兵线的移动，原因很简单，领土争夺模式中（其他模式不太好玩，也很少有服务器开设），进攻方要赢必须拿点，防守方要赢就必须要守点，双方围绕点位的争夺才是游戏真正刺激好玩的地方。所以建议刚入坑的玩家不要把这款游戏作为射击游戏来玩，射击只是游戏过程，团队胜利才是目的，你需要有一个大局观，多看地图，冷静客观地分析双方的交战形势、兵线的移动，思考对面可能的进攻与防守策略，根据自己扮演的不同角色去采取正确的行动，简而言之，不论你玩什么角色，你都需要把自己当作指挥官，从指挥官的角度去思考整个游戏，这很重要。
作为一款二战拟真游戏，红管2不如红管1的拟真度高，而是在多人联机与游戏的平衡和竞技性上下了功夫，理想化并简化了一些设定与操作，在游戏性与真实性上达到了不错的平衡。游戏中，由于地图和最大投送兵力的限制（32vs32，以人力数为增援，玩家可以重生，进攻方有红屏限制不能跨越多点进行完全的绕后包抄，游戏以这种方式刻意强化了每个点的争夺，牺牲了真实性换取了游戏的竞技性），这使得红管2变成了一款第一人称二战竞技场游戏。
游戏中的环境只有重力影响（弹道有下坠，人物会摔死）、简单的热力学影响（机枪会过热，但是其他武器却不会，这不真实）、没有复杂天气影响但有一些简单的光学变化（枪口焰、太阳光、爆炸、烟幕、雾气）。游戏中的士兵是完全理想化的战士（只有体力和负重限制），人手一份实时地图，全队可以语音交流，有侦察机提供敌人位置（不能提供掩体中的敌情），战场几乎是完全的信息化战场。即便如此，游戏的对抗性还是很强，防守方相较于进攻方有天然优势，当然这也和玩家水平有着密切联系，这里不得不提的是双方指挥官的炮击是改变战况平衡的最重要的砝码，炮击能显著改变双方在单位时间对目标点的投送兵力，从而改变形势。当然也和地图也有关系，有些图因为地形的原因，炮击不是很管用，还需要玩家们对地图的理解和相互协作。但是双方玩家之间的斗智斗勇都是为了一件事，提高己方对目标点的单位时间兵力投送值。（游戏中占点时的人数比就是双方数值大小的实时比较和反映）
游戏中，战场氛围的烘托很好，人物有精神值设定（精神值为0就会白屏），低人物等级玩家面对炮击时会长时间白屏，就算是英雄兵眼前有友军倒下也会瞬间白屏，人物模型塑造很细腻考究（人物穿着上，德军衣服上有铁十字勋章，苏军有共青团徽章，美军英雄兵有丛林迷彩，日军英雄兵的脚上是地下足袋，还有很多细节不一一例举了），作为一款11年出来的游戏，以当今的视角看其画面也许一般，但也正是这有点糙和昏暗的画质突出了一种浓浓的历史沧桑感。四个国家不同的战斗bgm时代感与特色非常鲜明，德军有一首优势下的bgm甚至借用了贝多芬的Egmont序曲的开头部分；苏军的劣势bgm，不仅元素多变，应该是四国劣势bgm里音乐元素最为丰富的，而且一听就是大祸临头的感觉；美利坚精神、昭和精神不用多说，一听就懂；当然随着游戏时间的增加，你会逐渐将bgm音量调低（战斗优先）。游戏中人物战斗时的吐槽和死亡时的骂街，也是对战场氛围的直接烘托。炮击中，你只能在白屏中看着自己的队友被炸的血肉横飞；一颗手雷过来，来不及跑就只能看着自己残缺的尸体了；在敌后穿插，被自己人打死早就是家常便饭；战斗是残酷、血腥的。
游戏中的人物动作设计不完全，下肢的动作并未完全设计好（拼刺出刀的一瞬间你会无法行动，人物僵直，趴在角落里你的双脚甚至可以挤上天花板）。网络不好时，你在翻越障碍物，说不定就会掉入异世界，而且无法改出。趴在层次不齐的地形里，你可以透视看到不应该看到的地方。但这些bug还是无法掩盖这部作品的优秀，这应该是我玩过的最优秀的二战历史向多人联机游戏。
苏德两方的炮兵火力总体来说区别不大，你有喀秋莎，我也有41式自走火箭炮，当然每张图略有区别，迫击炮、榴弹炮威力完全一样，每张图间隔时间也基本相同，炮击的伤害就完全看指挥官的能力了（游戏中迫击炮、榴弹炮、火箭炮安全距离分别为30m/50m/至少60m，火箭炮散布不规则、杀伤半径大但不能杀伤永备工事内人员，呆在工事内记住不要贴着窗户边）。
坦克方面，德军坦克有4号G（早期型）、3号M（无裙板）两种，苏军坦克有T34/76(T34 1942)、T-70两种。游戏中双方坦克只有AP（反装甲）与HE（高爆）两种泛泛而分的弹药（不可能跟WT一样，游戏中，德军炮镜上虽然有写弹种，但是车组装弹时AP与HE的炮弹模型是一样的，坦克的操控方式和WT的全拟真类似（你只能从坦克内部向外观察，坦克内部情况可视）。从整体上讲，德国坦克相较苏联坦克，主炮更为优秀、穿深更高、装填更快（4号比t34装填快一秒，t-70装填速度与德国车基本一致），先手能力强；正面防护上，德军坦克虽然采用了垂直装甲但只要会摆角度（3号M正面还有附加钢板），苏军也很头疼（两家主炮差距明显），t34与t70正面均有倾斜装甲（t34的倾斜装甲非常魔法，有角度的话跳弹概率极高，相比WT有过之而无不及），使得德军在正面面对苏军坦克时几乎只能攻击炮塔（炮手位），极大地提升了整个车组的生存能力；机动方面，4号与t-34几乎不相上下，两辆车巡航速度基本一致（接近40km/h），极速的话t-34略高，加速性能t34要优于4号，但整体操控4号略优（4号5人车组，t-34为4人车组），3号与t-70相比也大相径庭（但是3号的整体性能与战斗力远远优于t-70，t-70车组只有2人，3号为5人车组）。德军装甲车为Sd.Kfz. 251（Sonderkraftfahrzeug 251），苏军装甲车为通用运兵车（Universal Carrier，一说布伦运兵车，英制）。德军装甲车防护相较苏军会好很多（虽然AT枪随便穿），运载量更大（游戏中没太多明显作用），最大速度、巡航速度与苏联车相同（接近40km/h），但是车身狭长，不如苏联车灵活，转弯时丢速度不少。苏军装甲车短小精悍，车身结构紧凑（AT枪命中一发运气不好能穿死半车人），机动十分灵活（可以执行一些非常规战术），转弯时不丢失速度，车载机枪（无后座dp28）的左右射角与俯仰角相比德军装甲车要舒服很多。个人观点，苏军装甲车相比德军装甲车作用更大。
反器材武器方面，苏军为西蒙诺夫PTRS-41，德军为PzB 784(r)(PTRS-41的缴获重制版)，两家性能完全一样，100m垂直穿深大约为40mm左右。游戏中为单人携带与操作（这不符合历史），备弹较少，子弹初速非常高，威力惊人，命中即死。两种装甲车在这把枪面前都是裸奔，4号、3号、t-70的侧面、t34的侧面底盘都能做到100m内垂直一发穿。
半自动与栓动武器方面，双方栓动与半自动武器威力基本相当，kar98与mn9130半斤八两；svt40在供弹方面优于g41； tt33与c96单发伤害相同，顺枪速度差异不大(满级c96为双手持枪，对拼身体截面大，tt33为单手，身体截面小，两货都要压后坐)，有效控制范围都在50m左右，远距离散布满级c96略好，且满级c96有100发备弹，有快慢机，可以靠射速弥补精度的不足，提高控制范围，但是重量大影响行动，并且你有mp40会用c96吗，想用c96的人能活到开火距离吗，所以只能说单论手枪性能满级c96第一。
自动武器方面以班组机枪为核心步兵战法的德军火力占优。波波沙射速、顺枪速度均优于mp40,但有效控制范围在150m内，逊于mp40的250m；mkb42射速优于avt40，单发伤害逊于avt40，声音辨识度也极高，容易被针对，avt40的双发爆炸式开火于远于近散布都极佳，命中上身即死，且满级avt40的3.5x镜，使得这把枪的有效控制范围能够达到至少350m，这是mkb42做不到的。机枪方面，德军mg34无论射速还是精度都优于dp28，mg42射速非常霸道、精度略逊于mg34，瞬时射击密度极高，能抓到一些几乎不可能的窗口且附带压制效果，真正的战场撕肉机。但是游戏中还是做了平衡，dp28虽然从头到尾改装件并没有什么变化，只有47发弹盘但是队友可以直接补充，但是德军的两挺机枪初始都是50发弹鼓且满级mg34不打完一条弹链、满级mg42不先打完第二条75发弹链队友无法补充，这也算是一种平衡。德军机枪视野良好，火力强，压制时间持久，续航差，过热快。苏军机枪视野良好，火力不强，后坐不小，压制时间有限，过热慢（只有一根枪管，打坏了补给点也没法修），续航一般，适合进阶玩家练习枪法。总体而言，苏军支援火力与单兵火力都不输德军，班组火力逊于德军，两家各有特点，机枪方面，德军优势明显，胜负之事取决于玩家对游戏的理解以及相互配合程度了。
火炮方面，美日火炮优势取决于地图，总体而言趋于平衡，美帝的火力不符合历史（瓜岛美军只有迫击炮而日军有舰炮，其他图日军炮兵火力都不占优（大部分时候是这样，但也取决于日军掷弹筒的发挥），双方迫击炮、榴弹炮、舰炮威力相当，安全距离分别为30m/50m/至少65m。舰炮覆盖面与杀伤半径均大于东线火箭炮，散布同样不规则，同样不能杀伤永备工事内人员）。游戏中，与东线不同，双方均没有装甲战车的支援。
轻武器方面，美帝对日军是绝对的火力优势。美军除了春田、m12堑壕枪为单发栓动/泵动武器外（近距离m12几乎是不用瞄准的流氓枪），其他都是半自动或自动武器（不要怂，就是突突突），勃朗宁m1919轻机枪无论是视野、火力、压制范围与时间均优于日军没有满级的两把机枪（满级96、99机枪会有2.5倍镜，然而连狙作用有限），勃朗宁m1918 BAR是发射全威力步枪弹的自动步枪（瞬时射击密度很高，打中非要害部分，不缠绷带都有可能流血而亡），m1911作为一款传奇手枪更是全游戏单发威力最大的手枪，火焰喷射器的存在使得日军集团冲锋几乎是不可能。反观日军，除了南部100、南部14、96与99轻机枪为自动或半自动武器外，就只有寒酸的有坂38与99、刺刀与武士刀了（当然部分地图日军突击兵名额比较多，能弥补一下火力上的劣势），这也与日军精准击杀、崇尚拼刺的落后作战思想有关，游戏中日军的改装件也是这样，步枪改装给刺刀，机枪改装给刺刀，冲锋枪改装也给刺刀，就差给89式掷弹筒上刺刀了。所以单兵火力上的不足，使得日军在总体上非常依赖步炮协同，即机枪、掷弹筒、小队长、指挥官的火力协同，机枪与掷弹筒对团队的贡献还非常不稳定，取决于玩家的水平和游戏小时数。
但是游戏毕竟是游戏，既然要玩刀，制作组还是buff了日军，给了日军万岁冲锋的加成（万岁冲锋时，日军进入精神狂热状态，抗白屏、体力消耗速度减少、且拥有一件昭和避弹服！万岁冲锋的buff效果与人物等级、人数均有关，人物等级越高越明显，小队长与指挥官在时有叠加效果，最高加成人数为5人，同时给予美军昭和精神の压制。美军玩家近距离面对单个挥持武士刀的日军玩家或者集团冲锋的日军时都会白屏（作用效果依据美军玩家人物等级的不同也有差异）。5人加成的昭和避弹服的效果非常魔法，这件避弹服可以使你的头部等要害能在机枪火力不是非常非常密集的打击下得以幸存，即便是大出血也能有机会缠个绷带，继续战斗。所以，在游戏中，日军的集团冲锋可以使单个的美军火力点丧失原有的作用，但是火焰喷射器（敌我不分，粘到即死）除外。
既然谈到拼刺，这里就不得不说一下游戏中肉搏战（melee combat）的机制。游戏中的近身攻击武器按照打中非要害的威力排下来为武士刀、各种不同枪上的刺刀、各种枪托、手枪底座和望远镜，武士刀与刺刀还分别有轻刺与重刺（端着刺刀冲刺过程中可以点击鼠标右键直接取消冲刺但不取消奔跑）。肉搏中，双方的伤害结算不是非常好说，情况也非常复杂，这里只能说一些具体的经验。首先，伤害的结算与双方的体力值有关，双方同时使用重刺命中要害（双方都使用刺刀），体力少的那方一定判定死亡，体力多的一方则有可能出现多种可能情况，延迟半秒毙命（同归于尽，服务器延迟问题）、缠绷带无效站在那儿流血而亡（刺刀与身体碰撞体积的问题，双方身体靠的很近，服务器判定刺刀碰到了要害但不是从刺刀尖贯穿而过）、缠完绷带走人（1.网络延迟问题；2.服务器刺刀与身体碰撞体积的判定问题，你的刺刀感觉上是刺到了要害但实际上在碰撞体积边缘擦过，无效）。其次，还要看你的身体部位之前有没有受过伤，双方体力一致都是轻刺要害，你这个部位之前大量出血过，不管体力多少，你多半是要挂了。最后，看双方肉搏武器的伤害差异，你望远镜，人家武士刀，这就很尴尬了。综合以上三点，既然肉搏战不是一个稳定的判定，能不进入近战就不要进入近战，进入狗斗（dogfight）就意味着你的注意力没法放在战场形态感知上（就跟玩WT一个道理，狗斗穷一生），狗不赢大概率逃不掉，并且很容易狗进人群，被乱枪打死。不管是狗赢了还是狗输了，你接下来的生存概率都很低，又不是线列步兵时代的战斗，能用枪就用枪吧，尤其是新手。如果实在被人突进到跟前了，也不要脑子一热往上怼。首先，如果你对拼刺没有自信，能跑就往队友那里跑，召唤队友一起打死他，这种情况在低人物等级玩美军面对武士刀的冲击时尤其适用。如果实在没有办法了，那就只能狗了，狗斗时的情况非常多，但是不管对面时武士刀还是什么，都不要怂，随机应变，核心战法只有一条，骗敌人出刀（给对面一个假窗口，出刀的一瞬间人物会有僵直，后摇有长有短，越有经验的敌人后摇时间越短，但不管怎样总会有那么一瞬间的机会，至于怎么骗，这个只有靠经验了），在敌人抡空的一瞬间利用对面无法行动的窗口进行反制（1.躲避窗口时，一定要注意多观察地形，注意敌人的动作和想法，小心敌人的预判刺，尤其是面对日军时，日军装备负重低，刺刀长；2.不要心急，一次不行，多周旋几次）。所以如果你非常喜欢白刃战，交战前，请保证三点，自己的体力优势、躯干部分尽量不要有重伤、有一个不太差的白刃武器。
美军的总体战术执行起来就非常灵活与轻松了。对于火力上占绝对优势的美军来说，交战的主动权永远在我这儿，想怎么打我说了算，打不打的赢那另说。这里说几种思路，比如，进攻时，
1.小队长个人能力出众，能够突进到敌人点后，不断放人，以优势火力切断敌增援路线，友军分队以极小伤亡控制阵地；
2.小队长围绕喷火兵打，小队长以烟幕掩护喷火兵快速清点，小队成员以单兵火力优势控制阵地，日军掷弹筒与机枪手能压制我方，但逆转不了形势；
3.小队长因为种种原因放弃前两种战术，围绕机枪兵打，选择与日军进行对射，以烟幕掩护小队成员进点强攻，日军掷弹筒、机枪与炮击对我方威胁极大，虽伤亡惨重，但小队成员能在我这儿复活，以人数波次与单兵火力拼赢；
4.小队长与其小队成员均无法突破敌人阵地，被压制在敌阵地前，向指挥官请求炮击援助，随后完成进攻任务。除非双方玩家实力配比实在差距过大，或者地图偏袒日军（比如瓜岛），否则不会出现日军能先手压制美军的情况。

Should I play this game?

Depends on what you're looking for.
This game is a time killer, nothing more.
It's not exciting, unique or rewarding enough to keep you engaged for more than a few rounds.
The game is just a rinse and repeat of every match.
Load into the game... Check
Hunt the monster down for what feels like forever... Check
Have one player stupidly solo dome the monster... Check
Have the monster hump your face one at a time while your team bumbles about... Check.
PROS;
-The game looks nice.
-Feels responsive
-Effort was put in when designing the creatures and hunters.
-Witty dialogue makes for a good laugh
-Game has high success rate in placing you in your desired role
-Grouping up with friends and communicating makes for the best enjoyment.
CONS;
-Match macking is shotty, the game attempts to merge parties, but ends up dumping your friends out of the lobby. It can take anywhere from near instant to 10 min to find a party.
-Unrewarding. You can do very well in a match and only walk away getting 100 Silver keys(in game currency). You get 500 for leveling your account up, for a total of maybe 1000 keys here and there after the match.
-There is no way to preview the abilities or looks of any hunter. Do I want this hunter? I wonder what the weapon looks like while firing? Does it look good in game? Will I actually like the abilities once I use them? No way to tell in game without buying. At 5500 (average) that's a risk. If you don't enjoy the hunter, you've wasted your time.
-Monsters may feel overpowered. Oh, look, your tracker didn't track the monster very well, or at all in some cases. The monster hit level 2 and has come to wipe your team. You couldn't solo carry your team, you die, gg.
- Roles might feel too specialized. While most would argue that each player should be/can be doing their job, quite a few don't and probably never will. Oh look, our DPS/healer/etc was not in the dome when it dropped, he's 150 meters off trying to play catch up. What do we do? Guess we let it hump our faces since we can't put any meaningful dps on it, and dropping the dome would be grounds for instant flaming.
Now, not every game will go down like this, but after several hours/days and 15 levels, this happens more so than not.
The devs could allow for players to buy keys to unlock stuff. Sure, it's a microtransaction, but if you pay $5 for a hunter, you're supporting the devs. Noboy is forcing you, and buying has no advantages over unlocking if you simply wish to play the game.

Perhaps unknown to most, Aquaria is the touching tale of a girl who finds herself lost and alone.  In an effort to be reunited with her mother, Naija sets out to overcome the creatures in her world and rediscover her past.
Primarily a cursor controlled adventure, Aquaria melds elements of exploration, crafting, and combat to create a surprisingly rewarding experience.
That said, Aquaria is not for everyone.  Those searching for a quick pick-up-and-play title bursting with energy and excitement may feel somewhat let down by the game's more relaxed pace.
In the end, Aquaria is the perfect game to play at the end of a long day.  It's hand-drawn visuals and underwater melodies are sure to draw the player in, given the proper time.  Ultimately, your experience with this game depends on your play style.  If you have the time and like the trailer, you'll probably enjoy this title; to everyone else, keep searching.

I wanted to love this game, I really did, but it's just average and can't recommend for any particular interest. For a game about piloting giant robots, you'll find yourself surprisingly unempowered. Note that this is my first Front Mission, unlike most reviewers I've read.

Gameplay is average. Controls are pretty responsive however there's no strategy or thinking at all for the fights. There's no cover system, enemies can pack a punch really early into it and your weapons deal little damage (except for your rockets that are incredibly OP) so it's just "get behind a building. poke out, shoot a little, enter again. Rinse. Repeat." Your mobility is limited by a boost bar so it's just short bursts (dodge) or slow walking instead of a fluid movement system. (There's a burst for movement but it's pretty useless for fights).
You'll find yourself lacking either agility or power constantly through tedious levels.
Level design is good enough.
Bosses are surprisingly even more uncreative in terms of gameplay. You're just in a cage (you don't feel yourself in danger, just limited) where you dodge predictable attack sequences and shoot. If they were a little more open or interesting (in terms of enemy attacks/level design) I'd love them.
Story was pretty OK up to the point I got to. Nothing groundbreaking, but nothing really bad either. I've heard many complaints in this particular area so maybe it gets worse later, but I haven't found anything terrible yet, just cliches and "could have been done better" moments. Anyways don't play for the story alone.
Customization is decent, but not great.
Soundtrack is Okayish... Does it job, but nothing groundbreaking either.
Multiplayer is as dead as it can be. Don't even bother looking for a game.
If you want an action robot customization game, just go play Custom Robo. If you want a strategy robot customization game, just go play Super Robot Taisen. If you want a shooter... Well, I don't know, but this is not the game for you sadly.

Back in 2000, CogniToy, now defunct, released a strange game called Mind Rover: The Europa Project. This game was of a genre I call a programming puzzle game. The object was to build a little car to complete certain tasks. However, the only thing you could do is put sensors and switches on your car and wire them together creating a program. After that, the car would run the course and either succeed or fail based on your program. Others have tried but not succeeded the way Mind Rover did, at least not for me.
Fast forward ten years and Indie studio Zachtronics Industries released SpaceChem. While the premise is different, the concept is the same: a programming puzzle game. In this game, you are a SpaceChem engineer whose goal is to program reactors to take input molecules and output other molecules. The goal is to create a reactor program that runs as efficiently as possible: fewest code instructions, fewest cycles and in production puzzles - fewest reactors.
The screen is split into a grid 20 by 20 squares. On the left are two inputs (alpha and beta) 10 by 10 each on the right there are two outputs (psi and omega) 4 by 4 each. There are two waldo’s, one red and one blue, that execute your program. During every cycle, the waldo’s move one square along the drawn route and execute the action (some actions, such as rotation, take an extra cycle count), if any, in the square. Each square can have one action and one redirection for each color. Actions that you can do include getting an input from the input feed, clearing the output reactors, rotating a molecule, bonding (or de-bonding) molecules together, sync the waldos’ movement. One other rule - molecules cannot bang into each other. From there, you create the program to complete the task, run the program, tweak the program, and around and around until you are satisfied.
Running through the campaign, there are several different modes: Research, Production, and Defense. In the research mode, you have one reactor in which to take the inputs and make the outputs. In production mode, you have a planet view in which there may be many inputs to many outputs. You have the ability to create multiple reactors (level dependant) and pipe them around the planet. In this case, the movement of molecules through the pipes costs one cycle count. The final mode is the last mode for each planet and is a modified production level in which there is a specific goal and sometimes a time limit. After you finish the campaign mode there are some other puzzles that can be completed for added challenge.
In all modes except defense, there is a graph that shows the results of your program. This shows how many cycles it took, how many reactors (1 on Research puzzles), and how many symbols used (every redirect or input counts as one). The big kicker is that is shows where you stand versus other players, and here is where the ultimate tweaking and optimization comes in. Slight changes in order of operations, distance waldos need to move, which waldos are waiting during sync instructions all of these can have drastic changes to how fast your program executes.
I don’t know what it is about this game, but there are a couple of layers of challenge for me. On the first level, I just want to get a solution. The learning curve is fairly steep and there isn’t a user manual. There are about 10 tutorial missions, and the research usually gives some hint as to things you may need to use in future missions, but the puzzle difficult ramps up fairly quickly. The second is to optimize my solution. Moving things around and changing the order of operations can shave cycles off as well as reducing the number of symbols. The next optimization is to watch the reactor and see if one of the waldos is spending too much idle time. If so, can it be doing another task. This is easier to do in research puzzles as there aren’t restrictions on inputs and outputs. However, in production puzzles the reactors must wait to be fed (which takes time) and output pipes can only hold so much material. These reactors may stall while waiting to complete an instruction and in doing so create a jam. As you progress, you learn little tricks to get things to work more efficiently. These can be used in earlier puzzles to greatly improve times on earlier puzzles.
I know that this type of game isn’t for everyone, but I love getting into the game and tinkering and tweaking on puzzle solutions to make it 2 cycles faster (obviously more is better, but any little bit is a victory). If you are a fan of puzzle games or like programming (even better if you like both) then I would suggest giving SpaceChem a try

I had to write a review to counter all the negative reviews this game has been getting lately.
A lot of people are saying the devs have been promising to add a lot of features that never get added, but from what I've seen they have been bringing several new people in to help with development recently, so I'm optimistic about the future of this game.
For a top-down game with very simple graphics it's surprisingly realistic and challenging. When I'm walking the streets I really get a feel that I'm in a post-apocalyptic world. When you're looting houses it's almost like you can tell what kind of person lived there. Some houses will have lots of good books/magazines while other's will have a lot of electronic parts. I really like how the world seems to deteriorate the longer you survive. Grass will begin growing into the roads, vines will consume buildings/houses and you will see walls begin to crack.
The survival aspects of taking care of your character are also very realistic. You will have to keep them entertained if you stay indoors for too long so your character doesn't get sad/depressed. Eating healthy will help you heal faster. First aid mechanics are really good too. If you climb through a broken window there is a chance you will get a piece of glass lodged in one of your appendages and you will need tweezers to pull the glass out before it will ever heal. If your character is in pain you will need sleeping pills to help you sleep.
They do need to hurry up and add vehicles though, the world is so big that a form of transportation seems required to see everything.

In Karate Master 2 Knock Down Blow you take up the quest of a visionary man (Player 1) on his quest to open up his own karate school.  The reason why Player 1 wants to open up a karate school is so that he can pass down his style of karate (which is identical to the style used by every other karateka in the game).  Being that his city only has 10 karate dojos (other than the one he wants to buy and open) and 4 dedicated karate tournaments, there is obviously a vast untapped market for Player 1's tutelage.
There are two main ways to fufill Player 1's dream: putting boxes on a truck with a forklift and getting famous enough to participate in the advanced karate tournaments that actually have monetary prizes and don't cost money to do.  In practice, even if you opt for the second way of raising the necessary funds, you will have to do the forklift minigame every few attempts at the tournament.  Much like the path of a real karateka the game is very grindy and repetitive, but you'll have some fun if you buy it on sale.

After having enjoyed The Cat Lady, which is another dark, twisted game from the same developer, I got curious to try this one and was not disappointed at all. Downfall takes place in the same universe as The Cat Lady, with some common characters and happening almost in parallel to the events of The Cat Lady. Here the story revolves around Joe and Ivy Davis, a couple who have decided to take a weekend getaway in a nice hotel to rekindle their romance and fix their marriage. Except things quickly start going south and the place appears to be full of creepy and disturbing occurrences. When Ivy goes missing, Joe decides to do whatever it takes to find and save her.
The game is full of disturbing scenes and dark themes, a lot of the time making us ponder about the morality of what we're doing and whether what we're seeing is real or just a twisted figment of the character's imagination. The atmosphere is absolutely superb and immersive, often successfully creating tension and horror, and all this without using jump scares. The visual style is really great for a game like this, where even by the mere look, something can appear to give a chill down your spine. This is of course accompanied by a great soundtrack as well and some pretty good voice acting.
Most of the gameplay consists of solving simple environmental puzzles, exploration, and making choices, particularly during dialogue scenes. So it's very story-driven and casual as far as gameplay goes and should satisfy anyone who likes interactive stories. Most puzzles are pretty logical and straight-forward (though I did have to refer to a walkthrough at one point).
Your decisions have an effect on the ending you get, and there appear to be 3 endings in total, though the very good and the very bad endings are pretty hard to achieve and might need a walkthrough at hand or consecutive playthroughs.
Definitely recommended for anyone who likes darker stories that explore serious themes. If you liked The Cat Lady, you should enjoy Downfall too, and likewise if you enjoyed this, check out The Cat Lady too. As far as I've heard, there's another game in this universe currently in the works, so I'm very much looking forward to trying that out.
What a freaking journey... 9/10

I absolutely adored The Cat Lady for its atmosphere, art style, game mechanics, characters, and thematic elements, and it's become one of those games that resides in my heart as a personal favorite as a result. The Cat Lady, for all its flaws, really hit me with its ability to tackle a heavy subject and twist it with dark magical realism, horror, and metaphor within a skeleton of the frightening and drudging world of mental illness. As such, I jumped on the chance to play Downfall as soon as I learned that it was from the same group.
Downfall puts you in the middle of the story as Joe, a man who's dragged his wife to some hotel in the middle of nowhere in the hopes of fixing his marriage from falling apart. Much like The Cat Lady, you are not granted the knowledge of what the characters' backstories are immediately, and it is only through your way of progressing through the game and through your dialogue choices that you both learn and craft what their pasts really are. It's not like Telltale where it claims that your choice of dialogue matters a lot, but like in the Cat Lady, it makes you forget whether you're playing the game as yourself with the main character as an avatar (and thus crafting the character's responses and thoughts as you would for yourself) or if you're playing the game as the character and trying to get them to the end of the story relatively intact. I personally find myself combining both tactics in order to play these sorts of games, and they've worked well for me so far.
There are several endings that can be acquired, quite a few secret achievements, and a story that slowly begins to take shape just as everything else becomes fuzzier and fuzzier in regards to what is reality and what is hallucination. This is a game where your choices do matter in the long run, and I played my first time with that in mind and got a bittersweet ending as a result.
In regards to the story as a whole, it's very intriguing, dark, and chock full of those elements that made Silent Hill so good. I would not call this game a rip-off, just like I wouldn't a show like CSI a rip-off of Law and Order: The two operate on similar grounds and approach things in a similar way, but they are their own shows. The same goes for Silent Hill and The Cat Lady/Downfall: Both series make the player take the role of a character who, depending on their subsequent actions in the game, help you personally color what kind of person they are in reaction to, and in spite of, the mistakes they made that led them to experiencing the events in said game. Psychological horror, body horror, metaphors for what lurks in the minds of those haunted by themselves, a story in the past that unfolds as it does in the present, and the confrontation of real-life nightmares are what can be found in The Cat Lady/Downfall as much as Silent Hill.
The animation is much more fluid than The Cat Lady. While in The Cat Lady the characters moved a bit like paper cutouts (which is a nice stylistic choice, I thought), in Downfall it's Flash (I believe) and the movements are fully animated. They are shaded as three-dimensional, their chests visibly rise when they breathe in their idle state, and the head bobbing that came with the dialogue of some characters in The Cat Lady is gone. Glaringly, though, dialogue still does not quite match up with the lip movements, and this is even harder to ignore because Downfall has more scenes where there are closeups of peoples' faces when speaking, whereas in Cat Lady you stood a good 15 feet away at almost all times.
The design and art is a mixture of depressing, macabre photo realism, surreal imagery, and detailed animation. The game tries to use as limited and muted palette as possible - pretty much everything is a dour gray, black, and white except for the blood and some other accents. Agnes looks gorgeous and walks gorgeously in her wedding dress; the dilapidated areas of the hotel are well designed and reminiscent of Silent Hill 2 if they had been rendered in this art style and made by this company. The thick lines, detail, and subject matter reminds me of a combination of Archer, Adult Swim, and film noir.
As for voice acting... I feel like it was much stronger in The Cat Lady. Voices are monotonous in Downfall, almost painfully so, except for the Queen of Maggots and Agnes. I just can't ignore the lack of *oomph* in the voices when the subtitles clearly show that emphasis is supposed to be given to certain words a la ALL CAPS. Characters maintain an even, conversational tone (perhaps slightly inflected with a tiny bit of emotion) when the choice you made, subtitles, and situation obviously calls for the volume of one's voice to be kicked up a few notches. Honestly, it's like watching someone play Guitar Hero and miss half the notes on Normal mode - Dude, just stick to easy mode if you suck that much. For all of the missed cues to get emotional, the voices for Joe and Ava are decent enough: Joe (if you play him right) seems just as depressed as his surroundings but has a very soothing, if droopy hound dog kind of voice. Agnes has enough range of emotions to her voice that it almost makes up for the fact that everyone else seems to be stuck in 1st gear when it comes to emoting. Come on guys, you're not on camera so you have to put your feelings INTO your voice, like Agnes is!
If you loved the Cat Lady, consider this a phenomenal spiritual successor that must be played.

I need to open the review with a disclaimer: i've never played the original Downfall, so i can't make a comparison between that and the remake. I'll just make a few points against it and The Cat Lady.
First off, i sort of enjoyed playing the game, although i often felt like there were quite a few areas where it could have been polished or just done differently.
The plot is a quite compelling story that's a mix between reality and hallucinations ( i would say?), it basically depicts the events before The Cat Lady, and pretty merges with it at the end.
Visually, i haven't really liked some of the style which isnt also very consistent between different areas of the game, some scenarios involve basic 3D modeled backgrounds, while others offer much more detailed and coloured handmade artworks. The animations also kind of sucks, it's neither smooth or well done, and considering that Joe and Agnes move in the same way for like, 95% of the time, creating a couple of decent animations would have been a good idea...
Anyway, for the most part, the concept behind the scenarios and the overall game works pretty good. It lacks quite a bit of colour, especially in comparison to The Cat Lady, but it somehow still works.
Voice acting: aside of the overall incosistencies on the audio volume between different characters (some are too loud, some can barely be heard), i don't like Joe Davis's voice a lot, but considering that he's the same guy from The Cat Lady i guess that must be the way it has to be done...i actually liked more some of the minor char' voices, like the dead ones, or some female char ones. Even Agnes's voice isn't bad. Ivy's voice is a tad too muffled maybe.
Soundtrack wise, you do get to listen to some melodies, almost none of the pieces from the soundtrack is sung, and especially there is no recognizable voice over all of the tracks (which is sort of what worked quite well in The Cat Lady). Definately a bit of a shame, even if the soundtrack isn't really bad on its own anyway. It just doesn't make a lot to underline some particular events or some actions you happen to execute (aside of the killing).
About the interface...nothing has changed since The Cat Lady, apparently.
I would score this game at about 7.5 - i recommend it, although not to everyone as i would with The Cat Lady.

**********************************************
This Review has been completely rewritten after the following occurance:
Shortly after sending out my review the Dev responded with a little explaination of some of my mentioned negative points.
After that the Dev proposed that we'd play together. And so we did. A few other random people joined as well, so the multiplayer is not as dead as I initially experienced. It just took a few minutes.
Because this Developer actually takes his time to interact with his players and clearly has a passion for his own game, I decided to review this anew. However, know that I'm not gonna make a biased review. If the Developer takes his time to interact, I will take my time to nit-pick the hell out of the game. The Good, the Bad and the Ugly. Although the Rating changed from "Not Recommended" to "Recommended".
**********************************************
For the sake of sanity, I will make this Review more traditional in that I will make Bullet-Points of things positive, negative and meh. ("meh" can include things that are individually "negative" or "positive")
The Positive:
1. This game features rather simple control mechanics as seen in virtually every single flash-game 2d shooter to date. So if you played those you pretty much know the control-scheme. Which is a plus for convenience.
2. Pixely Graphics have 2 upsides to them: 1. It reminds us of glorious retro-games and 2. It is not so heavy on your graphics card. So, if you have an older computer (with sufficient RAM), you should've no Problems running the game.
3. As a Multiplayer-game this title shines, It is loads of fun to run around, shoot Zombies (and occasionaly other creeps), help each other out, try and get somekind of advantage before returning to your group to kick some more Zombies A**. The Dev himself described this game as a "multi-player-game in its core" and I agree. As a Co-op title this is a definite recommendation, as long as you like "Zombie Shooters". And Co-op.
4. There are excessive gamefeatures which, ignoring the fact that you need so called ZKW-points to unlock them (not to be confused with micro-transactions, you cannot buy ZKW-points), add customization and choice to the pretty simple genre of "Zombie Shooter". There are Maps, Perks, Weapons, Weaponupgrades and more to unlock.
5. In addition there is a skill point system for more basic boosts, like more Money per kill or more damage through melee. All this translates to both, single- and multiplayer, with only rare exceptions.
6. In-Game there are also mutliple options for the player to take. There are generally a good number of ways to spend money on the map, either buying weapons, upgrade an existing one, get a random powerup etc. Also, Power-ups like Shield and Health, that are picked up by one player count also for the other players, which reinforces group-support.
The Negative:
1. I said it in the original Version of this Review, and I'll say it again, the Reset Button on Weapon Upgrades is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. All it does is give you a Textbox stating "Are you sure? You will not get your ZKW-Points back." There is no friggin' point in resetting then, in fact, it has no benefits and just makes your situation worse than it was before. Which brings me to my second point... (It shall be mentioned that the Dev already responded to that, it shall be fixed in the upcoming version. But please, don't remove it, instead make it give us our ZKW back)
2. In such a game the Reset button on all and everything should be included. A Player just doesn't want to start all over, just to try and make a better Skill-Selection, Perk-Selection, Upgrade-Selection than before. What the player wants is his put-in Gamehours being worth something. This also wouldn't hurt the game and, in my humble opinion, would benefit the game and it's player. Let me Reset my spent Skill-points and spent ZKW-pts (excluding disposables of course, which can stay). Let me experiment.
3. The Character Menu is a little confusing. By just looking at it one would assume, that there are only 4 options in customization and upgrades, when in fact there are more. By clicking on a selection below the first you'll notice the Menu to kinda "roll" and present more options at the bottom.
The "meh":
1. ZKW-Points..... oh well, see, the ZKW-Points look like something bad, you might see it and think "oh... oh no. No, no, no, no. Micro-transactions!!!! Run!!!!", but you would be wrong. There are no Micro-Transactions (as of now). ZKW-Points could be most accurately translated to "multi-purpose Upgrade-Point". And they're aquired through gameplay and gameplay only. To quote the Developer himself: "As for ZKW-Points. You get these from: level ups, trophies, daily missions, challenges, and generally surviving"
2. I don't like some things that fall under "purchasable" in this game. While with things like Perks and Weaponupgrades it makes sense, you also need ZKW-Points to purchase Customization Options for your Character as well as any Level beside the first one. So you suddenly have to decide, if you want to be more competitive against the Zombies, or you wanna look cool or try a new Level (which is a thing that should be given to the player as a reason to keep playing). Here, a character-level based unlock-structure would've made more sense. Note: In Multiplayer all the Levels are accessable.
3. If you generally hate Online-Multiplayer and don't intend to play this game with friends either, be warned. While it is generally possible to aquire a good load of ZKW by playing Multiplayer, it would require quite alot more of single-player effort to get enough ZKW for decent progression, if you never touch multiplayer. However, if you aquired quite alot of ZKW-Points through Multiplayer, this also boosts your single-player competitiveness as well as your ability to aquire said Points on your own. In Short: Mixing multi- and singleplayer this is still a good and fun game, playing only and exclusively single-player turns it into a grind.
4. This game has issues regarding the "Grand Chase-Syndrome" (aka. Elsword Syndrome). This descibes a Situation, where having a pretty High-Level player in the group can really help out alot with a given level, but on the other hand, the challenge for the other players is spiraling down. Though the other players don't feel useless in this game, like they do in Grand Chase / Elsword, they're still majorly helpfull to the highlevel player, but a more challenge-hungry party of players should try to be around the same character level (+/- 5-10 Lvls)
5. I also imagine it to be quite fun to specialize with it's group, meaning, that one dude would concentrate on the skills and perks which gives him more money, to open doors, activate jump-fields and such, the other dude would specialize in Melee, while another goes for Ranged Weapons, each of which then would stay away from purchases other than the ones helpful to their role. This however would be made much easier a group-dynamic to provoke, if skills, perks and Weaponupgrades were resetable.
This concludes my Review of this game. I tried to be constructive and hope I've succeeded in that. Would I recommend the game? Hell Yeah! But not to people who really can't bare the thought of playing Multiplayer. All others should definitely check it out, if money allows. Time should not be an issue, one session will rarely take longer than half-an-hour and if it does, it's probably because you're having fun.
Best Regards,
Krolan

Hard to be decent when you first start out, but once you become adept at the game's core mechanics, you will have a grand time! The bullet snaps, whistling of artillery, whines of mortars, and shouts of courage or fear from your teammates easily have a gravitating effect of pulling you into the world. When every man counts, the matches can get exceptionally close. While the game has a heavy emphasis on teamwork, and communication, even just one player can make the difference between a victory or defeat.
Whether playing Rising Storm (Pacific Theater), Red Orchestra 2 (Russians versus Germans), or the Heroes of the West mod (Americans versus Germans), you will always feel like you are in the middle of the action. The emphasis of roles in the game account for the game's versatility to suit any fps fan. Snipers main job is to take out enemy machine guns, while machine gunners suppress the enemy, and keep an area pinned down. Squad Leaders act as mobile spawn points for their squad with Squad Leader 1 being the single most important role in the game. The Team Leader directs the platoon in battle plans, calls in recon planes to reveal enemy positions, and fire support when, and where needed. Lastly is the Rifleman. The Rifleman is the backbone of the platoon responsible for eliminating enemies, but moreso for obtaining the objective. No matter how you like to play fps games, this one will have a role for you.
The beautiful scenary, historic maps, accurate weapons, and sense of comradery granted by the small, yet passionate community gives the game the most exhilerating gameplay, and experience of any fps I have played. While you hide behind a building waiting for your commander's order to push the enemy, your squadmate is behind cover, yet exposing himself enough to engage the enemy, when all of a sudden he gets hit. As he is lying on the ground slowly dying in agony, crying for his mother, your commander orders everyone to attack. Not for the faint of heart, the game will bring you to the battlefield if you let it.
